{"slug": "website-builder-for-accountants", "title": "AI Website Builder for Accountants: Launch in Minutes", "metaTitle": "AI Website Builder for Accountants: Launch in Minutes | Kodely", "metaDescription": "Describe your accounting firm and Kodely builds a real, professional website with services, credentials, and a contact form then publishes it live free.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for accountants", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

What Accounting Firm Websites Actually Need

Most accounting firm websites fail at the same four things: they don't say clearly what services the firm offers, they bury the credentials that actually build trust (CPA, EA, CMA, state board licensing), they skip the trust signals prospective clients look for before handing over their financial life, and they make it hard to actually get in touch. A prospective client landing on your homepage during tax season isn't browsing they're deciding whether to call you or the firm in the next search result.

That means an accounting firm site needs to answer, in under ten seconds: what do you do, who are you licensed by, why should I trust you with my numbers, and how do I reach you today.

Must-Have Sections for an Accounting Firm Website

  • Services tax preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, audit support, business formation, advisory. List them specifically; "accounting services" alone tells a visitor nothing.
  • Credentials and certifications CPA license and state, EA status, professional memberships (AICPA, state CPA society), years in practice.
  • About / team real names and photos build more trust than a stock-photo hero image ever will.
  • Trust signals client testimonials, industries served, associations, and clear privacy language for anyone submitting financial documents.
  • Contact phone number and address above the fold, plus a contact form so visitors can reach out without leaving the page. This should read as a real invitation to talk, not a footer afterthought a "Book a consultation" form works well here.
  • Pricing or engagement approach even a general range or a "free initial consultation" line reduces the friction of that first call.

A Real Example Prompt for an Accounting Firm Site

You don't need a spec document to get a usable first draft out of Kodely. One clear paragraph in the chat is enough. Here's a prompt that produces a solid starting point for a small accounting firm:

"Build a website for Larkspur & Cole CPA, a small accounting firm in Denver, Colorado run by two licensed CPAs. We serve small businesses and individuals with tax preparation, bookkeeping, payroll processing, and business advisory services. Include a homepage with a clear services overview, an about page introducing both partners with their CPA credentials and years of experience, a services page that breaks out each offering separately, a testimonials section, and a contact page with a form for scheduling a consultation. Use a navy and warm gray color palette that feels trustworthy and professional, not flashy."

The more specific you are about services, credentials, and tone, the closer the first generation lands to something you can publish with minor edits rather than a full rebuild.

What Kodely Generates From That Prompt

Kodely turns that description into a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application actual .tsx component files built on a hand-built foundation of UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav), not a static HTML template and not a mockup. You get a working, navigable multi-page site: a homepage, an about page, a services page, and a contact page with a working form UI, all styled consistently from the palette and tone you described. The live preview shows the actual compiled app updating as it's generated, so you're looking at the real thing from the first draft, not an approximation of it.

Worth being precise about what this is: a professional marketing and informational site services, credentials, testimonials, a contact form. It is not a booking system, a payment processor, or a client portal. If you need clients to actually book appointments or pay invoices online, that still runs through whatever scheduling or payment tool you already use; the site's job is to present your firm and get the inquiry started.

Customizing Your Site in Chat

Once the first draft is live in preview, refine it the same way you built it by describing the change. "Add a section listing the industries we specialize in, including restaurants and medical practices." "Make the about page lead with our combined 30 years of experience before the credentials." "Change the contact form to ask what type of service they're interested in." Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes, and every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint if a change doesn't work out, rolling back to the previous version is free and immediate.

You can also open the code view at any point to see and copy the actual source files Kodely generated, useful if you want to hand a snippet to a developer or just understand what's under the hood.

Publishing Live

When the site is ready, publishing is one click. Kodely puts it live on a real public URL in the form yourfirm.kodely.site no separate hosting setup, no extra cost, and every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally-leaked API keys or secrets before it goes live. Your accounting firm can be live on the web the same day you started describing it in chat.

Kodely runs on credits tied to actual AI cost signing up gets you 750 credits free, no credit card required, and a build that fails to compile is never charged. If you need more after that, top-ups run $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (most popular), or $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code to build my firm's website with Kodely?
No. You describe the site in plain English and Kodely generates the real code. You can view and copy the source if you want it, but nothing about publishing requires touching code.

Can Kodely add online booking or invoice payments to my accounting site?
Not yet. Kodely generates the frontend a professional services site with a contact form for consultation requests. It doesn't generate backend systems like booking calendars, payment processing, or client portals.

Can I use my own domain, like larkspurcole.com?
Not currently. Published sites live on a free yourfirm.kodely.site subdomain.

What if I want to change something after the site is published?
Describe the change in chat and Kodely updates the real components. Every generation creates a checkpoint, so you can roll back for free if you don't like a change.

How much does it cost to build a site?
You start with 750 free credits, enough to generate and refine a full site with no card required. See pricing for top-up details if you need more later.

Ready to see your firm's site take shape? Build your accounting firm site free and describe it in your own words the first draft is minutes away.
